How important to you is your view out your windows? Do you care what you have to see outside, our does it not matter as you always have your curtains closed anyway? What is your current view, and how would you like it to change?
How important to you is your view out your windows?

A view out the windows is nice, but I normally have the blinds closed for privacy and to keep light out when I'm sleeping. Part of what sold me on where I live now is a view of the Western sky from the patio deck. It is nice to see the sun go down from time to time. I wish I could knock down a few tree branches to see the sky better but alas, the tree does not belong to me.

I had a nice view of the western sky from my bedroom window where I lived about 15 years ago and it must have made an impression on me. What is also kind of interesting is that the view of trees and grass from my bedroom window now is similar in scope to the view from my bedroom window when I was growing up. That is, there is a similar amount of trees and grass and the trees are about the same height. There must be some subconscious desire to recreate my childhood home I guess.
What part of your childhood do you miss the most?

Overall I would say a tighter-knit sense of family and friends. I remember being very sad when my brother went off to college because it meant the end of this idyllic world I grew up in. With regards to the physical aspects of where I grew up, I would have to say just have trees to look at out my bedroom window.

It's dark in the expanse of the sea with a slight twinkle in the waves from the moon when it peeks out from behind a dark cloud.

The only thing I would change is that my eyes be closed and my mind quiet so I can sleep. Otherwise, it's beautiful.
I'd like to have a lot of property in a wooded area not too far from where I live since most of my friends or family live within 2 hours away. But wooded property around here Is kinda pricey
The window views have never been that important to me. But now a days I have a great view of the mountains from my patio window, so that's cool.

Like most ancient people, we have a ton of 8mm home movies. I spotted a film scanner on that place we're not allowed to link to for $150, so I thought it would be cool to scan a bunch of the old movies for the Mrs and my mom.

Got the thing, and it's a nice design except... no motor drive. It's primarily designed as a negative scanner, so the user is expected to advance the film frame-by-frame by hand and push a button to scan each frame.

I DON'T THINK SO.

Okay, it's a fair misunderstanding... I wonder what one with a motor costs.

...

...

They don't exist.

The options appear to be either this or a $2,000+ contraption that's basically a digital camera stuck on the front of an 8mm projector, which means you have to have a damn movie projector running all day to scan movies.

And digitizing services run $15+ per reel.

What am I missing? Obviously we have cheap technology that can get a frame of 8mm film onto digital media, so what's the problem with getting a bunch of them in a row? Is the whole world stuck on synchronizing the frames? Because that's stupid - just scan the entire length of film and assemble it digitally - find the frame borders (easy), snip into jpgs (easy), assemble into MP4 (easy).
Why is scanning Super 8 / 8mm film so hard?
$15 per reel is not that bad

Except I've got 40 reels. While I probably don't want all of it, I was really hoping to get it all into digital form so I could just edit it in Premiere (as opposed to trying to pick & choose by unspooling film). If I had a device where I could throw a reel on and forget it, then I could just have it at my elbow while I'm doing something else.

I would try and work out a deal based on the fact that you would be bringing a bunch of reels in. I would bet you could get them down half. Meanwhile, all those memories are fading. Have you checked Walmart or Costco for a better price?
